evidence: Cascade Falls, Rogan's Gully (the gully left of the falls) and Urs Hole are neighbouring Cascade Mountain flows above the Trans-Canada, all in the Avalanche Canada ice atlas / Mountain Project Cascade Mountain ice listings (https://avalanche.ca/resources/ice-climbing/atlas/rogans-gully, https://www.mountainproject.com/route/113838560/the-urs-hole). Named for the falls; a specific sub-face name was not confirmed.

Louise Falls, Cable Gullies and Dark Nature are all at the far end of Lake Louise (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/107474498/lake-louise-ice, https://avalanche.ca/resources/ice-climbing/atlas/louise-falls). Dark Nature is described as a chasm across the slope from the falls; 'Unnamed' has no source, kept with the group.

All 11 routes (Nemesis, Suffer Machine, Fiasco, Rhamnusia, etc.) are on the Stanley Headwall itself per https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106927666/stanley-headwall and https://avalanche.ca/pages/suffer-machine-man-yoga; no finer named sector found, so named the face (parent is the Headwall, and the rock sibling is separate).

Heart Creek Falls is the waterfall at the head of the Heart Creek canyon walk (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/heart-creek-falls/107390061; Alberta Parks trail report). Warm-up Ramble not found in any source; kept with the leaf.

Single route Amadeus (WI4 M5, 2 pitches). Search placed it only vaguely (one user list shows it under a Cascade Falls sub-area; Mountain Project filed it in Kananaskis 'Unsorted Ice routes'). No confirming source of a place, so left as is for manual review.

Marble Canyon ice and mixed (Icy BC, Body Shop, Deeping Wall, Comfortably Numb) is on the cliffs on the SW side of Turquoise Lake, reached by walking across the lake from the campground (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/122569467/marble-canyon-ice, https://summitpost.org/icy-bc-area/880792). Name is a judgement call; Pink Cadillac and other mixed lines not individually confirmed.

Waterworld is the roadside viewpoint/access trail on Hwy 23N at the south end of Lake Revelstoke; routes are named Waterworld North Ice (local guide, seerevelstoke.com). Dam Falls and Kokanee Falls siblings are separate flows. 'Spider in the tub' unplaced, kept.
The one route, Oregon Jack WI4, is the ice on the falls of Oregon Jack Creek in Oregon Jack Provincial Park (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/108298349/oregon-jack).
Candy Box is at Copper Mountain, Terrace, via the power line access road (https://www.mountainproject.com/route/118342107/candy-box). The AKA Coffee Burp route was not found; kept with it.

moves.evidence: Route name is Olesen Creek slabs; sibling Olesen Creek is a leaf 0.5 km away
Mountain Project coordinates put it near Olesen Creek (https://www.mountainproject.com/route/125605779/stranger-than-frictionless-ice)

evidence: AMO Slabs is the real feature name; Left AMO Slab stays. The two moves rest on name and coordinates, not an explicit place statement.

moves.evidence: Low confidence: no source names the cliff; Sunnyside Wall is the main wall of the area

evidence: Mountain Project sunnyside ice area holds only these 2 routes (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/117700967/sunnyside-ice); no source places them on a specific cliff, so moved to the main wall. Flag for review.
Searchmont Ice Wall is a real named wall (routes Left, Right Side, Mixed Wall are on it); Searchmont is a known Algoma ice destination (destinationontario.com). Kept.
Lost Falls is the named place; the single route Coloured Anatomy sits under it. No web source found for the route itself.
Single route Studs Ahoy WI3 at 48.302,-89.239 near Thunder Bay; no source found naming a more specific crag. Weak name, flag for review.

Routes (Where Egos Dare, Tammy Baker's Face, Kermit's Finger, etc.) are on the cliff at Diamond Lake near Combermere (https://gripped.com/?p=46834, Mountain Project trip report). No sibling uses the name.
